sourceChecks.title: What Could Self-Healing Metals Mean for the Future of Engineering?
sourceChecks.excerpt: fatigue cracks in pure metals can undergo intrinsic self-healing
sourceChecks.paraphrase: ANSI reports that the cited Sandia/Texas A&M study observed spontaneous healing of fatigue cracks in pure platinum and copper during nanoscale experiments, described as crack-flank cold welding.
sourceChecks.limitations: This is a standards-news summary of nanoscale pure-metal experiments, not structural alloy validation; it states practical manufacturing applicability remains unknown.

sourceChecks.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for High-Strength High-Entropy Alloy Design
sourceChecks.excerpt: Here we present a framework to predict and optimize the yield strength of face-centered cubic (FCC) HEAs
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The preprint reports a model combining composition and processing parameters for FCC high-entropy-alloy yield-strength prediction; it gives R²=0.915 and reports experimentally examined candidate alloys.
sourceChecks.limitations: Case study is limited to selected CoCrFeMnNi-based HEAs and yield strength. It does not establish first-principles prediction of arbitrary property combinations or instant universal alloy design.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: experimental machine learning alloy design composition processing primary alloy paper

sourceChecks.title: Microstructural Investigation of Oxidized Complex Refractory High Entropy Alloys
sourceChecks.excerpt: After oxidation at 1200°C for 10 hours, a distinct aluminosilicate layer could be observed
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Two experimental refractory HEAs formed aluminosilicate layers after 1200°C/10 h oxidation; the paper reports those layers were discontinuous and the internal oxidation zones porous.
sourceChecks.limitations: The results do not show stability above 1600°C, long service life, strength retention, or coating-free performance in turbine/hypersonic conditions.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: refractory high entropy alloy oxidation 1600 °C primary study

sourceChecks.title: Directional Solidification of Single-Crystal Blades in Industrial Conditions Using the Developed Gas Cooling Casting Method
sourceChecks.excerpt: Five blades from the mold for each process were then selected to examine the dendritic microstructure
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The paper experimentally compared industrial-condition directional solidification methods for single-crystal superalloy blades and measured dendritic microstructure differences across blade regions.
sourceChecks.limitations: This is a specific alloy and blade process, not meter-scale crystals, arbitrary compositions, zero defects, or improved creep/fatigue life.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: single crystal turbine blade industrial casting defects primary study

sourceChecks.title: Recycling of Aluminium from Mixed Household Waste
sourceChecks.excerpt: the alloy composition of the remelted metal is dependent on decoating temperature
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Experimental remelting of household-can aluminum found yield, dross, oxide inclusion content, and alloy composition depended on decoating temperature; higher temperature improved yield/inclusion content but reduced magnesium.
sourceChecks.limitations: One scrap stream and a small experimental series do not establish unlimited closed-loop cycles, original-property restoration, all engineering alloys, or the stated carbon/mining impacts.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: repeated recycling property retention steel aluminum primary experimental study

sourceChecks.title: Unusual super-ductility at room temperature in an ultrafine-grained aluminum alloy
sourceChecks.excerpt: to attain elongations to failure of > 150% while retaining the enhanced strength
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The indexed abstract reports a 2010 aluminum-based alloy processed by severe plastic deformation with room-temperature elongation above 150%, attributed to grain-boundary wetting/sliding.
sourceChecks.limitations: This database reproduces an abstract rather than the full article. The result is below 1000%, concerns a specific processed Al-based alloy, and does not establish low-cost repeatable superplasticity in ordinary steels or Al alloys.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: room temperature superplasticity aluminum alloy 1000% elongation primary paper

sourceChecks.title: Revealing the room temperature superplasticity in bulk recrystallized molybdenum
sourceChecks.excerpt: with a maximum of 108.7% obtained after 1200 °C annealing
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The authors report recrystallized bulk molybdenum samples with room-temperature elongation up to 108.7% after annealing.
sourceChecks.limitations: This result concerns pure Mo, not low-cost ferrous/aluminum alloys, and falls short of the >1000% milestone.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: room temperature superplasticity metal 1000% elongation alloy paper

innovations.summary: A narrowed machine-learning alloy design study reported composition-and-processing-aware yield-strength prediction and experimentally examined candidates. It does not support the universal first-principles design engine or the time/impact forecasts.

claims.claim: Universal engine that outputs exact composition, treatment and microstructure for any requested combination of properties, with trial-and-error eliminated and development reduced from decades to days.
claims.scope: The read preprint addresses FCC CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys and yield strength, reports model R²=0.915, and reports experiments on generated candidates.
claims.limitations: It does not cover arbitrary alloy systems, property combinations, first-principles completeness, production qualification, or the projected industrial time savings.

evidence.supportedClaim: A model using composition and processing predicts FCC HEA yield strength and reports experimentally examined candidate compositions.
evidence.paraphrase: The authors report an FCC HEA case study, R²=0.915, and experimental XRD/SEM/tensile examination of two generated candidate compositions.
evidence.limitations: Specific material family and target property; preprint findings do not demonstrate universal first-principles alloy design.

searchLog.query: machine learning inverse design alloy composition processing experimental validation alloy paper

innovations.summary: A secondary institutional summary reports a nanoscale observation of intrinsic crack healing in pure Pt/Cu. Practical structural-metal self-repair remains unestablished in the readable material.

claims.claim: Autonomous room-temperature healing of fatigue cracks or voids in crystalline structural metals without external stimuli or rare elements.
claims.scope: ANSI says a cited Sandia/Texas A&M Nature study observed crack-flank cold welding in pure platinum and copper at nanoscale.
claims.limitations: The primary Nature page could not be read. The summary explicitly says manufacturing practicality is unknown; no structural alloy or service-life evidence.

evidence.supportedClaim: The ANSI report describes spontaneous fatigue-crack healing in pure Pt/Cu in nanoscale experiments.
evidence.paraphrase: The report attributes the observation to crack-flank cold welding and states that practical manufacturing use remains unknown.
evidence.limitations: Secondary report; nanoscale pure-metal experiments do not validate room-temperature healing in structural alloys or impact claims.

searchLog.query: metal intrinsic self healing fatigue crack pure platinum copper nanoscale experiments Nature 2023

innovations.summary: The bounded search found literature focused on fatigue limits and very-high-cycle failures but no inspectable primary result demonstrating infinite life under arbitrary cyclic loading. The universal “any loading” claim and impact forecast remain unsupported by this audit.

claims.claim: An alloy microstructure suppresses crack initiation and propagation under any cyclic loading in real engineering environments, producing true infinite fatigue life.
claims.scope: No inspectable primary result was located in the bounded search that meets this all-loadings formulation.
claims.limitations: Finite-cycle results, endurance limits, and particular test conditions cannot establish infinite life under arbitrary loading; the 10× weight and trillions forecast is also unsubstantiated.

searchLog.query: metal fatigue endurance limit very high cycle fatigue review primary experiment no infinite life alloy
searchLog.outcome: Bounded targeted search did not locate an inspectable source substantiating the exact threshold or universal formulation.

claims.claim: Defect-free amorphous parts above 10 cm, for arbitrary alloy compositions and sizes, with the stated mechanical/corrosion properties and impacts.
claims.scope: The relevant specific ScienceDirect article was found but could not be read.
claims.limitations: An inaccessible page cannot resolve whether its narrower experimental result supports any component; arbitrary scale/composition and zero crystallinity/gradients were not assessed.

searchLog.query: bulk metallic glass critical casting thickness arbitrary size composition primary study

innovations.summary: Two read abstracts report narrower room-temperature ductility advances: >150% elongation in a processed Al-based alloy and up to 108.7% in bulk Mo. Neither reaches the proposed >1000% low-cost steel/Al capability.

claims.claim: Stable repeatable >1000% ambient elongation in everyday low-cost steels or aluminum alloys without exotic additions.
claims.scope: The accessible EPA-indexed article abstract reports >150% room-temperature elongation in an SPD Al-based alloy; a primary Nature Communications paper reports 108.7% in annealed bulk Mo.
claims.limitations: The Al abstract is an index record, and Mo is not Fe/Al. Neither demonstrates >1000%, ordinary low-cost alloys, repeatability at scale, or claimed manufacturing/energy savings.

evidence.supportedClaim: The abstract reports >150% elongation at failure at room temperature for one SPD-processed Al-based alloy.
evidence.paraphrase: The indexed abstract attributes the elevated ductility to grain-boundary sliding/wetting while retaining enhanced strength.
evidence.limitations: Index abstract, one alloy and process; below 1000% and does not establish common low-cost steels or scale.

evidence.supportedClaim: In a distinct bulk Mo study, a sample reached 108.7% room-temperature elongation after 1200°C annealing.
evidence.paraphrase: The paper reports maximum RT elongation 108.7% in a 1200°C-annealed sample.
evidence.limitations: Pure Mo, not ferrous/aluminum alloy; below the proposed threshold.

searchLog.query: room temperature superplasticity metal 1000% elongation alloy paper

innovations.summary: The bounded search did not locate a readable primary result supporting absolute immunity to all corrosion modes across all environments. Corrosion testing standards and isolated resistant materials do not establish the universal claim.

claims.claim: Any alloy is thermodynamically and kinetically immune to oxidation, pitting, SCC, and hydrogen embrittlement in any environment, eliminating protection systems and global corrosion losses.
claims.scope: No specific readable primary study was found for the universal claim.
claims.limitations: The claim bundles distinct mechanisms and environments; no single narrow material test can establish universal immunity or the predicted economic effects.

searchLog.query: corrosion immunity passive film hydrogen embrittlement alloy all environments primary study
searchLog.outcome: Bounded targeted search did not locate an inspectable source substantiating the exact threshold or universal formulation.

innovations.summary: A read experimental study examined two refractory HEAs after 1200°C/10 h oxidation and identified oxide-layer composition and porosity; it also documents substantial oxidation limitations.

claims.claim: A coating-free class that retains strength and oxidation resistance above 1600°C in oxidizing atmospheres for turbines/hypersonics and raises efficiency 30–50%.
claims.scope: The primary study tests small ML-SP2/ML-SP2A refractory HEA samples at 1200°C for 10 h, reporting aluminosilicate surface layers, discontinuity and porous internal oxidation.
claims.limitations: It does not test >1600°C, mechanical stability/strength, turbine exposure, long duration or efficiency impacts; it reports limitations rather than qualifying the aspiration.

evidence.supportedClaim: Experimental oxidation characterization at 1200°C for 10 h reports surface-layer and internal oxidation behavior for two refractory HEAs.
evidence.paraphrase: Both alloys developed aluminosilicate layers, but those layers were not continuous and internal oxidation zones were porous.
evidence.limitations: Far below the >1600°C target; no retained strength or engine performance tested.

searchLog.query: refractory high entropy alloy oxidation 1600 °C primary study

innovations.summary: A primary study reports industrial-condition directional solidification of specific single-crystal superalloy blades, with microstructure varying by blade location and method. Universal, defect-free, meter-scale growth is unsupported.

claims.claim: A universal technique grows meter-scale, defect-free single crystals for any alloy; impact is 2–3× creep/fatigue life.
claims.scope: The read study compares Bridgman and gas-cooled directional solidification in industrial conditions for selected single-crystal blade castings, characterizing dendrites in five blades per method.
claims.limitations: It is limited to selected Ni-based blade castings and reports location-dependent microstructure; it does not establish meter-scale specimens, any alloy, zero defects, or the stated life multiplier.

evidence.supportedClaim: The study demonstrates industrial-condition production and microstructure assessment of specific single-crystal blades using two processes.
evidence.paraphrase: The authors examined selected cast blades and found dendritic spacing varied with blade thickness, location and solidification method.
evidence.limitations: Specific blade system and nonuniform microstructure; no arbitrary alloy, meter-scale, defect-free, or lifetime result.

searchLog.query: single crystal turbine blade industrial casting defects primary study

innovations.summary: A study of household-can aluminum remelting measured alloy quality and found that process settings changed yield, dross, inclusions and Mg content. It does not demonstrate property-preserving infinite recycling.

claims.claim: Unlimited closed-loop cycles restore original composition, microstructure and performance in all engineering alloys without virgin additions, producing the stated mining/carbon impacts.
claims.scope: The read experimental abstract covers decoated can scrap remelted in four ~2 kg additions per experiment and reports outcome dependence on decoating temperature.
claims.limitations: One waste stream and one recycle stage do not establish repeated-cycle property retention, all alloys, no virgin additions, or broad mining/carbon impacts.

searchLog.query: alloy recycling property retention repeated cycles experimental metals

innovations.summary: A specific primary quasicrystal study about small-scale room-temperature ductility was found, but the PMC article page was blocked. No inspectable evidence supports the proposed combination of bulk ductility, >50 GPa hardness, low density and scalable production.

claims.claim: A new phase combines >50 GPa hardness, >10% room-temperature ductility and density <4 g/cm³ at scale, replacing ceramics/composites.
claims.scope: The relevant specific PMC primary article was found but inaccessible through the page tool.
claims.limitations: The search-result text alone is not used as evidence; the title concerns small-scale quasicrystal ductility, but the full material and measurements could not be inspected.
